title: What runs when Spring Boot starts?
outcome: Explain how main(), the container, configuration, and the web server fit together.
cue: Boot builds the room. Beans are the people inside it.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: The app starts on 8081. A developer calls localhost:8080/ping and reports that the controller is broken. List two checks before editing the method.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: Add a /ready endpoint that depends on a fake store bean. Explain why creating that store with new inside the controller changes how it is configured and tested.

trace.title: main
trace.detail: Spring Boot builds on Spring. Spring manages objects called beans. Boot supplies useful defaults when the required classes and settings are present. This is auto-configuration. It can step aside when you define your own bean.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
1. The JVM calls main. Boot builds the context.
2. Component scanning finds PingController. MVC records its /ping mapping.
3. The server listens on the configured port. A request reaches the mapped method.
4. The method returns text. MVC writes the HTTP response.

Command-line properties override application.properties for this simple case. Profiles select environment-specific settings; they are not a place to commit secrets. Use the condition report (--debug) to see why a default was applied.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A controller outside the scanned package may never become a bean. A port conflict happens before a request is handled. A 404 after startup is a routing problem, not proof that Boot failed to launch.
